label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**One star for now: good software, but support has left us running a library on index cards**

I'm the director of Bridger Bend Community Library. We're a single branch with two full-time staff, a handful of volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. In June 2026 we signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud at $14,200 a year. Migration went live October 19.

Some fair credit first. The software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is better than our old system. My problem isn't the product idea. It's support.

Since October 28, checkouts only work offline on a single laptop. Our holds queue was wiped, roughly 640 holds gone. Last week a retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up the large-print Westerns he'd placed on hold. We had no record of them and had to send him home empty-handed. Our volunteer has been writing checkouts on index cards.

Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We've had three replies, and each one said "escalated to engineering." Before we signed, the sales rep promised us a dedicated migration specialist. What we got was a shared inbox.

The timing matters, too. Our line item is on the county budget agenda November 18, and I'll be explaining to commissioners why a system we're paying over $14,000 a year for can't check out a book.

**To Stackhouse leadership:** I'd like a named person at your company to call me this week. I don't mean another ticket update. I mean someone who can tell me who owns this problem and when it will be fixed.

**To other library directors, especially at small libraries:** Before you sign, ask any vendor to put its support response times in writing. Ask what "dedicated migration specialist" actually means and get the person's name. A small library doesn't have an IT department to fall back on when things go wrong, so the support commitment is the contract.

I'll update this review if Stackhouse makes it right. I'd honestly like to, because the software has real promise. For now, one star.

*Director, Bridger Bend Community Library*
